hypotheses: H1: The first line A375 yields a vehicle-norm activity label for each compound; a second line chosen for maximal tissue divergence (e.g., PC3 or YAPC) will more often produce a discordant label, increasing the count of compounds with one active and one inactive line.

H2: The first line A375 yields a label that is largely driven by shared systematic response; a second line chosen for similar lineage or target-expression context (e.g., MCF7 or HT29) will more often reproduce the same label, reducing discordance and thus the target count.
evidence_gaps: No measured activity labels are provided for any compound-line pair; only availability and first_line are known.
Target expression and dependence across A375, HA1E, HELA, HT29, MCF7, PC3, YAPC are not established in the sources.
The mapping from compound MOA/targets to L1000 activity is not validated; S5 warns activity is a vehicle-norm threshold, not viability.
It is unknown whether the first-line A375 label is active or inactive for each compound, so the required second-line choice cannot yet be optimized.
Source S2 suggests shared systematic response may inflate prediction quality, but its effect on cross-line discordance is unquantified.
